observation: A technically valid training path can still be the wrong production path when model scale, data scale, objective density, and evaluation quality are mismatched.
lesson: Preserve proven infrastructure and checkpoints, but redirect future compute when frontier comparison reveals a better capability-per-GPU-hour design. Do not continue a path simply because its launcher and checkpoints already exist.
application: N0 v0.1 step-1000 remains a pathfinder baseline. N0 v0.2 starts native random-init at a smaller compute-efficient scale, broader governed data, denser semantic objectives, and fixed invariance evaluation.

observation: Preference rows that store a rationale but train only on preferred indices teach outcomes without directly teaching the governing reason.
lesson: When the target capability is transferable judgment, make principles/rationales gradient-bearing through compatibility and contrastive objectives rather than keeping them as audit-only metadata.
application: N0 v0.2 adds candidate/rationale alignment and semantic/rationale contrastive learning while retaining listwise preference and span MLM.

observation: Repeatedly editing a tiny dev curriculum after observing failures turns evaluation into training and makes apparent progress hard to interpret.
lesson: Freeze a versioned benchmark before the production run. Test paraphrase and candidate-order invariance, and create a new benchmark version rather than editing the old one after seeing results.
application: N0 v0.2 freezes one unseen base case for each of 43 competencies and deterministically expands prompt and candidate-order invariance variants. Benchmark rows explicitly forbid training.

observation: GPU scarcity is best handled by a capability-per-GPU-hour policy rather than by repeated tiny qualification jobs or arbitrarily long continuation runs.
lesson: Remote accelerator allocations should produce durable checkpoints and material capability evidence. Set an explicit review budget and stop when fixed held-out gains do not justify more compute.
application: N0 v0.2 uses maximum 4-hour 2xP100 allocation units and forces an architecture review after at most 24 P100 GPU-hours unless fixed generalization gains justify continuation.
